At the SHIPPED arm a fork never changes a later decision, and presence_only — rejected here on a 2-question difference in one 3-person world — is nearly 4x the pre-flip arm. ⭐⭐ AND THE ZERO IS NOW DIAGNOSED, WHICH RETIRES THE ARM QUESTION RATHER THAN ANSWERING IT. description: H-71'S OTHERS HALF CLOSED, THE WRITER ONLY. `ED-IN-0245`/`CAT-6` (2026-09-17) closed the holder's own knowledge of a remit (arm 2, `Tenure.granted_acts`) and left explicit: "the half of H-71 about being UNDERSTOOD BY OTHERS as seated remains OPEN." `_eff_confer` (`engine/season/loop/effects.py`) reports the new `hold` Tenure's own hash id as what a `confer` changed -- correctly, that is what the gate actually wrote -- but `H-79`'s `per_change`/`both` claim-subject rule (`epistemic.claim_subjects`) deposited that opaque id UNEXPANDED on every admitted witness, a claim naming nothing any reader dispatches on (`_ch_document_key` reads a `hold` Tenure by `(subject, object)`, never by its own id). The Receipt itself is untouched and stays honest -- `e.changes` still names the Tenure that was actually written; only the WITNESSED CLAIM is about what the Tenure connects. This closure makes office-seating WITNESSABLE; it does not make belief in it fallible by channel, competence or prior belief -- that is separate, general, already-tracked work (the AX-7 channel-confidence item), not specific to this fact. A LIMITATION NAMED RATHER THAN FIXED: `_fold`'s `_apply_write` unions every EARNED kind's ids into one `changed` list before minting (`resolve.py`), and every earned kind's Event then carries that same union -- so conferring onto an ALREADY-HELD office would still leak a claim about the outgoing holder's Tenure onto witnesses of the closure alongside the correct one. THE CHARACTER MODEL AND THE DECISION LAYER, RULED BY JORDAN ACROSS ONE SESSION. One ruling event, one subject, one id by lane precedent (ED-IN-0233 covers two documents under one id; ED-IN-0244/0245 covered nine rulings across two). NOTHING IS IMPLEMENTED HERE: this records the rulings and lands the authoring surface they need. The rename, the cells and the verbs are R6-atomic and wait on the cells. 

THE BASIS. `Person.convictions` -> `Person.pursuits`; `conviction_axes` -> `pursuit_axes`. The rows are PURSUITS -- something a person is AFTER, not a position they hold -- which is why Authority, Precedent, Utility, Equity and Identity did not survive: they were institutional positions. FIFTEEN: virtue, honour, liberty, justice, wealth, reputation, scholastics, stability, individuality, community, faith, happiness, family, love, warden. SEVEN BIPOLAR AXES, both poles named: hierarchical/equal, precedent/substantive, partisan/equitable, selfish/selfless, rigid/flexible, grandiose/humble, deontological/instrumental. 

THREE NAMES WERE CHANGED AGAINST MEASURED COLLISIONS, counted on .py/.yaml over engine/season + systems + references, non-test. `status` (510 hits, the ubiquitous field key) -> `reputation`, which is CLEAN: all 25 hits are prose, and `options.py:477`'s `standing_of` docstring already uses 'reputation' as the CONTRASTING concept. `standing` was considered and REFUSED at 404 hits for a better reason than the count -- `standing_of` computes a GAP where low is good, so a pursuit of standing inverts polarity against it. `order` (442 hits: canonical order, act order, sort order) -> `authority` -> `stability`; `authority` was refused because #358 rev.2 s.E.2.2 rules AUTHORITY IS A PROPERTY OF THE SEAT BEING EXERCISED, NEVER OF THE PERSON EXERCISING IT, and a pursuit is by definition a property of the person. `stability` also fixes an independence problem `authority` had: you can want a stable EQUAL society, so it is orthogonal to hierarchical/equal in a way a pursuit of command would not be. `partial` -> `partisan`; `partial` collides with the requirements register's own state value (126 hits). ⚠ THE NAMING METHOD WAS PARTLY WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE: `names_index.yaml:127-128` already namespaces a busy word (`mech.stability` vs `fac.stability` vs `clock.ms`), so hunting for unused words was the wrong test for DATA. It remains the right test for PROSE and for polarity, which namespacing cannot fix -- and `Person.stance`, which has FOUR live senses and no names_index entry at all, is what happens without it. 

DROPPED. `Person.marks` -- a write-matrix row retired by W2 whose FIELD outlived it; zero readers, zero writers, no canon referent. `Person.orient` -- never built, and now redundant: self/other lives in the pursuit space (wealth, reputation, individuality against community, family, love), so a field would be a second home for one fact. `benefits_me` and the 38-row beneficiary column SURVIVE -- the selfish axis score supplies the disposition, the column the per-candidate fact. THAT DISSOLVES R7's OBJECTION rather than hitting it: R7 says a projected axis cannot vary at fixed weights, and it no longer needs to, because two people with identical pursuits ARE identically disposed and the variation comes from the candidates. `sacred` leaves the moral basis for `Person.conviction`, carrying religious affiliation intensity (R1/R2, ED-IN-0251) -- it was always a religious word in a moral basis. 

KILL / WOUND IS NOT A VERB, and the finding behind the ruling is larger than the ruling. MEASURED: only 2 of 38 verbs carry `contests` at all -- `kill / wound` -> the body, `tell` -> a standing -- and the personal-combat engine is registered `@provider('contest','personal_combat')`. So `kill / wound` is the ONLY route to it, and it is excluded from `resolvable_verbs` because its `requires` is `—` (driver.py:139 keeps Jordan's 2026-09-02 *you can't just kill or wound* true). CONSEQUENCE: THE PERSONAL-COMBAT SEAM HAS NO PERSON-SIDE DOOR -- nobody in a season can start a fight, because the only door to the fight is labelled with its result. The row was carrying the ATTEMPT's job because no attempt verb existed. RULED: `fight` (opponent is `subject`, needs a typed precondition or it fails driver.py:146 exactly as kill/wound does), and the duel pair `challenge` -> `accept`, with `accept` carrying `contests: "the body"`. `duel` is not a verb either: it is the name of what resolves. The seam wrapper is already verb-agnostic (it takes a prize and claimants and 'decides nothing itself'), so legibility was never the issue. `H-80`, filed to ADMIT kill/wound to resolvable_verbs, is refused by this ruling. 

DEONTOLOGY IS A REFUSAL AND IT GATES. Jordan: *it's a refusal to take certain actions. It gates actions insofar as the weighting is a threshold for certain actions.* So the weight IS the threshold and there is one mechanism, not two: a candidate whose `align(verb, deontological)` sits beyond what the person tolerates NEVER FORMS. Site is `opening_set(p, v, q, fx)` -- person-side, no World, AX-2 intact. `score` cannot express refusal: it ranks, and at tau=0.1 a good enough outcome outranks any finite penalty, so a deontologist as a score term is an instrumentalist with a strong preference. Jordan's own definitions, recorded because a prior session conflated them: deontological/instrumental is WHAT MAKES AN ACT PERMISSIBLE, precedent/substantive is WHERE YOU LOOK FOR THE ANSWER. Orthogonal -- all four corners are populated -- so a high measured `r` between them is a PLACEMENT defect, not a redundant axis. 

SCARS: THE DIAGNOSIS AND THE LAWFUL WRITE. The design (`conviction_track_v1.md` s2, quarantined, reference for intent) has scars accrue from WITNESSING morally-loading events, counted PER ELEMENT, with thresholds at 1 (destabilise), 2 (WEIGHT SHIFTS, others gain proportionally) and 3+ (crisis; terminal -- restabilise, fold, or be destroyed). THAT IS THE ONLY THING IN THE DESIGN THAT CLOSES THE DECISION LOOP, and the loop is measurably open: 2,403 forks reconverge 100%, later-decision divergence ~4%. WHAT WAS BUILT SUBSTITUTED ALL THREE LEGS -- trigger witnessing -> being wounded (item 21's L4 amendment), key per-element -> per-AXIS (`_scar` reads ALIGNMENT), and type COUNT -> continuous float (`scar_step x cell`). The third is why `scar_step` parked at 0 with no reader: it is a magnitude for a mechanic whose unit is 'how many times'. RULED: scars apply to BOTH tracks (pursuits AND convictions), the unit is a COUNT, thresholds 1/2/3. 

AND THE RESOLVE-vs-WITNESS QUESTION IS SETTLED RATHER THAN DEFERRED. L4 (holonic_ARCHITECTURE.md:173) constrains WHO writes, not WHEN: *`social: true` means ONLY AN ACT MAY WRITE IT*. At WITNESS the writer is the world processing an Event -- the violation item 21 names. At RESOLVE the writer is the ACT, which is lawful. And 'who witnessed' is NOT private to WITNESS: `epistemic.py:440 observers_for(w, e, mode, everyone)` is a STANDALONE function that WITNESS calls, so RESOLVE can call it too and there is one owner of perception (s8) rather than a duplicated predicate. Witnessing is already selective -- MEASURED: `fan_out_mode = all_five` is the shipped ruled default (2026-09-07, R7) over chronicle/co_located/document_key/post_remit/witness_key. SO THE LAWFUL FORM IS: at RESOLVE, after the act's Event is formed, the act calls `observers_for` and writes a scar on each observer whose pursuits or convictions that act violated. Item 21 was right that WITNESS cannot write it and wrong to conclude the scar must fall back to 'the outcome that names the person' -- that threw away the crowd to solve a problem the crowd was not causing. ⚠ DECLARED DIVERGENCE: `observers_for` at RESOLVE and at WITNESS can differ on `co_located`, because WITNESS is the join and a later act can move someone; the scar then reflects who was present WHEN IT HAPPENED, which is the more correct reading for witnessing but is a real difference between two calls to one function. 

ONE RECORD CORRECTED IN PASSING. `witness.py:94-95` asserted the channel predicates do not exist and the fan-out is therefore total -- false, and contradicted SIX LINES BELOW IT by `W6`/`H-33`'s own note. A reader taking it at its word concludes witnessing is unselective, which is how the scar mechanic came to be written against participants instead of observers. Same class as the six records ED-IN-0260 corrected. 

WHAT THIS COMMIT LANDS: the worksheet (`proposals/2026-09-20-pursuit-basis-worksheet.yaml`, 15x7 = 105 cells, alignment re-cell over 40 verbs, the scar model, and what is open), a supersession banner on the 2026-09-18 worksheet (kept because ED-IN-0251 R3 cites it and its religious cells carry forward), and the witness.py correction. WHAT IT DOES NOT LAND: the rename (483 occurrences in engine/season non-test, 392 in references owners; `registers/`'s 403 must NOT be rewritten, they are the record of what was said when), the 105 cells, the verbs, and the scar rebuild -- all R6-atomic and all downstream of the cells, which are Jordan's under STR-6/R3. MEASURED-BY: engine/season/harness/conviction_spread.py -- the instrument that scores any placement, reporting magnitude, within_60deg, pairwise r and participation ratio. 

AMENDED SAME DAY: `faith` KEEPS ITS ROW, ruled. `Person.conviction` is which side you are on and how intensely; the `faith` PURSUIT is how much of yourself goes into religious matters at all. Orthogonal -- intensely orthodox and never acting on it, or lukewarm with a life organised around church politics, are both expressible. Jordan verbatim: *"someone who is a devout church of Solmund follower want to do work for the church or someone who is pure Einhir and anti Solmund church whose faith work is about dismantling it."* ⚠ AND THE PAIR IS RECORDED AS THE PLACEMENT'S FALSIFIER RATHER THAN AN ILLUSTRATION: both score HIGH on `faith` and want opposite things, so only the AXES can separate them. That is precisely the discrimination ED-IN-0214 measured the old basis failing -- nine of thirteen rows within 60 degrees of one mean vector, so two people sharing a primary came out the same. After the 105 cells are placed, score the two; if they do not land far apart the placement is wrong, and `conviction_spread`'s `within_60deg` is the aggregate form of the same check. 

SECOND AMENDMENT SAME DAY, AND IT REVERSES THIS ROW'S OWN RULING. Jordan, after the row was committed: *"admit kill and wound as resolvable verbs."* WHAT THIS ROW SAID: *`H-80`, filed to ADMIT kill/wound to resolvable_verbs, is refused by this ruling.* THAT REFUSAL IS WITHDRAWN. What survives unamended is the rest of the verb ruling -- `fight`, and the duel pair `challenge` -> `accept` -- which was never in conflict with it: those are the acts a person DECLARES, and the admission is about whether the fold can carry a body-contest at all. The two answers are independent and both are now yes. 

WHAT WAS BUILT, AND IT RUNS (CLAUDE.md s0.2). `kill / wound` is in `resolvable_verbs()` -- 18 verbs -> 19 -- and EXECUTES IN 47 OF THE 89 LIVE CORPUS WORLDS. Until this commit `@provider('contest','personal_combat')` was registered and unreachable from a season: the personal-combat engine had NO PERSON-SIDE DOOR, which is the finding this row already carried. THE ADMISSION ITSELF IS ONE CELL -- a typed `requires` on the row (`existence` of `subject`, kind `Person`) -- because `driver.py`'s contest gate excludes a contested verb that is UNTYPED, on the ground that `operands_for` returns `{}` for one and the seam would get a single claimant. Typing the row binds `subject`, which IS the second claimant, so the gate's own recorded reason stopped holding. The clause is the narrowest that does the job and is not a stand-in: you cannot fight someone who is not there, and `Person.exists` is the field the `Felled` band writes. 

THREE FOLD DEFECTS HAD TO BE FIXED BEFORE IT RAN, EACH MEASURED, EACH AT ONE OWNER, AND ALL THREE WERE LATENT RATHER THAN NEW -- invisible for as long as no contested verb could be chosen. (1) `resolve()`'s CONTEST BRANCH SKIPPED ELIGIBILITY AND `requires` ENTIRELY. sE2's order is *eligibility -> requires -> resolve* and the branch is the alternative to `_fold`, which is where both checks lived, so a contested act was carried into personal combat without its precondition ever being read. MEASURED on admission: 85 of 143 corpus cases became whole-case DESIGN-GAPs, 74 of them PARTY-GAP -- *claimant not a person: 'p_a' / 'rec:cb377aad7694a2da'* -- because `opening_set` binds `subject` from the question's referent and a referent is usually a Record or a Rung. FIXED by extracting `_admits(w, a, row)` and calling it from BOTH paths (s8: one owner); a refused contested act emits `emits_on_refusal` and is witnessed rather than raising. (2) EVERY PERSON WAS OFFERED THEMSELVES AS AN ADVERSARY. `opening_set` offers every person themselves as a referent for every verb -- 49.6% of all candidates name the actor as their own subject -- so the commonest contested candidate in the corpus was a man attacking himself, and 47 more cases died on *personal combat needs two parties; got 1*. FIXED person-side, off the ROW'S OWN `contests:` column and never a verb name: a contest needs two claimants and a person is not their own adversary, which is `move`'s *a node is not a path to itself* one seam over. (3) A DEAD PERSON WENT ON ACTING, AND ALSO WENT ON BEING CONFERRED OFFICES. s27.1 says each act sees the world its predecessors left, and until a man could be killed inside the fold nothing tested what his successor does. Two faults, one root -- THE DEAD STAYED REFERENCEABLE: `World.remove_person` popped `persons` and left the person's own `person`-kind RUNG standing, which is exactly the id-scheme ambiguity `class_of`'s docstring warns about (persons is scanned first, so the id reads Person while they live and silently becomes Rung the moment they do not), and 11 cases died on `_refuse_bad_hold` -- *`hold` tenure has subject 'p_c', which is a Rung* -- because `confer` seated an office on a corpse; and 2 more (`ARC-10`, `ARC-12`) reached the seam with a dead FIRST claimant. FIXED at the two owners: the node dies with the person in `remove_person` (kind checked, not assumed), and the fold emits `act.ineligible` for an actor a predecessor removed. 

THE CORPUS RETURNS TO ITS PRE-ADMISSION BAR ON EVERY COUNT BUT ONE, both arms at seed 0 over the same 143 cases, control from this tree with the five files stashed: DESIGN-GAP 0 -> 85 -> 0, R1 89/89 -> 4/89 -> 89/89, UNREPRESENTABLE 54 unmoved. THE ONE EXCEPTION IS REPORTED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: `NPC-009` moves RUNS-UNDECLARED -> RUNS-ALONE-UNDECLARED, a death breaking that case's propagation, which is the mechanic working. SEVEN ARTIFACT NUMBERS MOVED AND EACH IS RE-PINNED WITH ITS CONTROL, NOT ADJUSTED: distinct executed sets 44 -> 57 (variety rose; the universal set `{create_record, utter}` was re-taken IN THE SAME BREATH and did NOT move, so this is not the `U1` shape); eight verbs reach fewer worlds for the scenes the contest takes, NAMED rather than netted off, AND SEPARATED FROM THE FOLD FIXES BY A THIRD ARM rather than attributed whole to the admission -- which is the correction a control bought and the two-arm reading had wrong. THREE ARMS, same 89 live worlds, seed 0: BASELINE (nothing) -> FOLD FIXES ONLY (the admission monkey-patched off at the loaded row, so `resolvable_verbs()` is 18 again) -> BOTH. The fold fixes ALONE move four verbs and move variety NOT AT ALL -- distinct sets 44 -> 44 -- `tell` 72 -> 70 (its precondition is now read BEFORE the seam, which is defect 1 biting the other contested row), `interview` 53 -> 57, `release` 10 -> 12, `research` 63 -> 64. THE ADMISSION IS WHAT MOVES THE REST, on top of that arm: distinct 44 -> 57, `interview` 57 -> 46, `tell` 70 -> 63, `speak` 82 -> 78, `move` 51 -> 47, `surveil` 58 -> 55, `transfer` 77 -> 75, `release` 12 -> 9, `research` 64 -> 63. That variety is the admission's and none of it is the refactor's; clause-4 drops 8 -> 9; `W-D` fork divergence at the `total` arm 7 -> 8 with the denominator unmoved at 31 -- MORE divergence, which is the direction R-01/R-02 want; maturation depth ceiling `depths[6]` 12 -> 11 (act-mix-driven by that test's own argument, and `depths[3]` unmoved is the control). TWO COMMITTED ARTIFACTS RE-RECORDED DELIBERATELY (`CASELOG_NPC.md`, `results.json`) and the re-record is the PAYOFF rather than bookkeeping: case rows reading *'kill / wound' is on the table and the fold cannot execute it* now read PASS, and `NPC-010`'s core_blocked falls 2 -> 1. CONTROLS THAT DID NOT MOVE, stated because an absence is the cheapest claim to make: the headless content hash is `80789994e376c5304c5f8acce4a3b4d7` before and after, `m1_acceptance` holds `ab77c30d273b` with 0 stub invocations, and 24 headless seeds x 4 seasons + 2 populated report 0 invariant violations over 16,194 events. 

WHAT IS STILL OPEN AND IS NOT THIS AMENDMENT'S. THE SLASHED NAME SURVIVES and is separately ruled wrong (*"kill / wound isn't supposed to be a verb by itself"*). Splitting it into `kill` and `wound` needs a row of ALIGNMENT cells each, and `ALIGNMENT` is being re-celled whole over the seven `pursuit_axes` -- so the split rides that commit, where the cells are authored once, rather than inventing two rows of four old-basis cells that are about to be deleted. `fight` and `challenge` -> `accept` ride the same commit for the same reason.
